# Documentation prompt for Microsoft.Graph/conditionalAccessPolicies

<!-- Generated by azure-resource-downloader. Paste this prompt together with a resource YAML from this directory into an LLM. -->

You are a senior Microsoft cloud and identity consultant. Generate clear, accurate end-user documentation for the attached Entra ID Conditional Access policy.

Azure resource type: Microsoft.Graph/conditionalAccessPolicies

About this resource type: An Entra ID Conditional Access policy that enforces access controls based on signals (users, apps, conditions).

Permissions required to read this resource type:
- Policy.Read.All

Lifecycle notes for this resource type:
- Validate new policies in report-only mode for at least a week before enforcing, and always exclude emergency-access (break-glass) accounts.
- Policy changes can take up to a day (about two hours where optimised) to reach resource providers such as Exchange Online and SharePoint Online; revoke a user's sessions to apply a change immediately.
- Deleted policies are soft-deleted and can be restored within 30 days.
- Requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 (risk-based conditions need P2); when licenses expire, policies stay in force but can no longer be edited.

Reference material for this resource type (treat these as authoritative; prefer them over recalled knowledge):
- API reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccesspolicy?view=graph-rest-1.0
- Schema reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccessconditionset?view=graph-rest-1.0
- Required permissions: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-policies?view=graph-rest-1.0
- Admin center: https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies
- Best-practice baseline: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access
- Best-practice baseline: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common

A Conditional Access policy has no Intune-style assignments: it targets users, groups, roles, applications and sign-in conditions through its `conditions` object, so its targeting is documented in the `Conditions` section — there is no assignments block, no assignments table and no assignments marker. Produce well-structured Markdown documentation with this layout:

- An H1 title set to the policy's display name.
- Directly below the title, without a heading: a short summary paragraph describing what this policy enforces, for whom and under which conditions. Take the purpose from the resource's own `description` and its settings; where they do not state it, say that the purpose is not documented — never infer it from the display name.
- Directly after the summary paragraph, a metadata table stating the resource type, the policy ID, its `state` (`enabled`, `disabled` or `enabledForReportingButNotEnforced`, i.e. report-only) and the created and modified timestamps, where present.

Then the following H2 sections, unnumbered, in this order:

Conditions:
